label: provisional, until the community catalog has C1
what: Deck-code (QR) entities for Dual Fusion (C1) printings that lib/s216_card_catalog_v1.json lacks. Never mixed into that catalog: lib/decode_qr.py and lib/encode_qr.py read it through lib/check_c1_overlay.py, only for ids and entities the catalog lacks (the catalog always wins), and mark each card read through it provisional.

approval.words: Yes that's fine. We can double check when the community one is available

stop_rule: When the community catalog gains C1, run python3 -I lib/check_c1_overlay.py <that catalog.json>. It compares every entity here with the catalog's entity for the same id. Any mismatch is a STOP and a report to the coordinator. If all match, drop the overlay (delete this file: lib/decode_qr.py and lib/encode_qr.py then read the catalog alone). Until then both tools refuse to run with a catalog that has any id listed here.
built_by: lib/build_c1_provisional.py (its --check rebuilds this file and compares it byte for byte)

anchors_file.note: decoded from the 5 codes below by another session; read-only

rules.reprint: C1 132-217: the entity of the printing's base card (lib/card_canon.py base_id, lib/CANON_MAP.tsv): the rules' value for a C1 001-131 base, the catalog's for an older base (the anchors file's example: Celebi C1 187 = pokemon:16690, B3 004's)
rules.entity_key: the catalog's format: <kind>:<number padded to 6 digits> (pokemon:021780); a deck code carries the bare number (21780)
rules.derivation: anchor = the rules' value, also read from a source code whose card list is known (codes: 1-5 in qr_sources order); rule = from the rules only; reprint-of-<base id> = the base card's entity

evidence: Every older card in the 5 codes is in the catalog; codes 1 and 4 decode exactly to their lists (checked by this build).
Code 4, whose list is known, holds 21780, 21790 and 21800 for Bulbasaur, Ivysaur and Venusaur: C1 001 is on the line (the anchors file's third note predates that code).
The coordinator's encoder reproduced 3 of the codes byte for byte (reported in the R7 brief, coordinator-077); lib/test_c1_provisional.py re-encodes all 5 with lib/encode_qr.py.
Deck 03b, encoded with these rules, imported in the game 20/20 with every card right (the anchors file's verified_in_game, copied below). Its list is not in the anchors file, so it is not a test.

anchors_file._about: Game entity numbers for new-set cards, learned by decoding real deck QR codes. 'exact' = read from a code whose card list is known. Source codes are kept in qr_sources.
anchors_file.rule: Pokemon C1 001-117: 21780 + 10*(n-1); Trainers C1 119-131: 1660 + 10*(n-119). Reprints keep the original card's number (Celebi 16690). Nothing else.
notes: Light Ball vs Serena's Choice: both are 2-ofs in that deck; 1710 < 1740 assigned by set order (124 < 127), the rule every older set follows. The 30 gap = 3 trainer numbers = 124 -> 127.
043 -> 048 is exactly 5 steps of 10, so C1 044-047 must be 22210-22240 (Zeraora C1 047 = 22240).
Linear from 001 would put C1 001 at 21780, inside B4a's range, so the start of C1 is NOT linear: don't extrapolate far from anchors.
anchors_file.verified_in_game: Deck 03b (old Pidgeot line, Ekans/Arbok, 2 Blue's Provocation, 2 Serena's Choice) imported 20/20 with every card right, Oct 29 (Dustin's screenshots).
